chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis

questions.chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis
questions.stem: An employee slipped on oil leaking from a pump. Which finding is most likely a root cause rather than an immediate cause?
options: The preventive-maintenance system did not identify or correct recurring seal failures
Oil was present on the floor
The employee shoe contacted the oil
The employee lost balance after stepping in the spill
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A root cause is an underlying, correctable system failure. Weak maintenance controls explain why the leak recurred and remained uncontrolled.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Oil on the floor describes the immediate hazardous condition, not why the system allowed it to persist.
Contact with the oil is part of the event sequence rather than an underlying system failure.
Loss of balance describes the injury mechanism, not the organizational cause.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 22, investigation procedures and causation models, pp. 515-536; OSHA Incident Investigation overview

questions.chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis
questions.stem: After emergency care is complete, what should the investigation team do before equipment is moved or production resumes?
options: Interview only the injured employee and release the area
Control the scene and document conditions, positions, and evidence
Discard damaged components to prevent reuse
Require the supervisor to reconstruct the event from memory
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Securing and documenting the scene protects evidence needed to reconstruct the event and test causal explanations.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A single interview cannot preserve physical evidence or capture all relevant perspectives.
Damaged components may contain critical evidence and should be controlled rather than discarded.
A memory-based reconstruction is less reliable than contemporaneous documentation and evidence preservation.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 22, fact finding and investigation procedures, pp. 528-530

questions.chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis
questions.stem: Which opening question is most appropriate when interviewing a witness soon after an incident?
options: Why did the operator ignore the procedure?
You saw the guard removed, correct?
Please describe what you observed from the beginning, in your own words
Which employee should be disciplined for this event?
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: An open, neutral invitation obtains the witness account without embedding assumptions or blame.
incorrectOptionExplanations: This assumes a violation and may make the witness defensive before facts are established.
This leading question suggests the desired answer and can contaminate recall.
Assigning blame is not the purpose of an evidence-gathering interview.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 22, interviews and fact finding, pp. 529-530

questions.chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis
questions.stem: Why should a failed lifting component collected after an incident have a documented chain of custody?
options: To determine which worker receives compensation
To replace the need for photographs and measurements
To guarantee that the component manufacturer is liable
To show who controlled the evidence and protect its identity and integrity
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A chain of custody records possession and handling so the evidence can be shown to be the same item and not altered or substituted.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Compensation eligibility is separate from evidence-control documentation.
Chain of custody complements, rather than replaces, other documentation.
Evidence control does not predetermine legal responsibility or product liability.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 22, fact finding and report of investigation, pp. 528-535

questions.chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis
questions.stem: A five-whys review ends with the statement, "The employee was careless." What is the strongest criticism of that conclusion?
options: It stops at a blame label and does not identify a controllable system condition
Five-whys analysis must always contain exactly five documented causes
Human actions can never contribute to an incident
The method should be used only for equipment failures
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A useful root-cause analysis goes beyond labels and identifies conditions such as design, workload, training, incentives, or supervision that can be changed.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The number five is a prompt for depth, not a rule that every analysis must end after exactly five statements.
Human actions may contribute, but the analysis should also ask why the action made sense or remained possible.
The technique can be used for organizational, procedural, equipment, and human-performance issues.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 22, problem-solving and investigation techniques, pp. 530-533; OSHA root-cause guidance

questions.chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis
questions.stem: Which analysis starts with an undesired top event and uses logical gates to identify combinations of lower-level failures that could produce it?
options: Job safety analysis
Fault tree analysis
Pareto chart
Gantt analysis
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Fault tree analysis is a deductive method that works backward from a top event through AND and OR relationships.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A job safety analysis breaks a task into steps, hazards, and controls.
A Pareto chart ranks categories by frequency or impact but does not use logical failure gates.
A Gantt chart displays project activities against time.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 22, fault tree analysis, p. 532

questions.chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis
questions.stem: A design team lists how each valve can fail, the effect of each failure, existing safeguards, and recommended actions. Which method is being used?
options: Event tree analysis
Management by objectives
Failure modes and effects analysis
Cause-and-effect interview
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: FMEA systematically examines potential failure modes, consequences, controls, and priorities for action.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Event tree analysis follows possible outcomes after an initiating event rather than examining each component failure mode.
Management by objectives is a performance-management approach, not a system safety analysis.
Interviews may supply evidence but do not provide the structured component-by-component method described.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 22, failure modes and effects analysis, p. 532

questions.chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis
questions.stem: Following a solvent release, an analyst maps whether detection succeeds, isolation succeeds, and ignition occurs, producing different outcome branches. Which method is this?
options: Fault tree analysis
Descriptive statistics
Job hazard analysis
Event tree analysis
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Event tree analysis starts with an initiating event and follows the success or failure of subsequent barriers to possible outcomes.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Fault trees reason backward from a top event rather than forward through success and failure branches.
Descriptive statistics summarize data and do not model sequential barrier outcomes.
A job hazard analysis examines task steps and controls rather than branching event sequences.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 22 and 35, system safety analysis methods, pp. 532-533 and 793-794

questions.chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis
questions.stem: A team separates filter replacement into shutdown, isolation, opening, removal, installation, and restart, then identifies hazards and controls for each step. Which method best fits?
options: Job safety analysis
Fault tree analysis
Cost-benefit analysis
Emergency action plan
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A job safety analysis breaks work into steps and evaluates the hazards and controls associated with each step.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A fault tree models combinations of failures leading to an undesired event, not sequential task steps.
Cost-benefit analysis compares monetized alternatives and does not identify step-level hazards.
An emergency action plan addresses emergency reporting, evacuation, and related duties.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 22, job safety analysis, p. 531

questions.chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis
questions.stem: A suspended load falls into an unoccupied barricaded area and no one is injured. What is the best investigation decision?
options: Close the event because there was no recordable injury
Investigate the event because the potential consequence was serious and the control failure is actionable
Record only the crane operator name for future discipline
Wait for a similar event involving an injury before investigating
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: High-potential near misses reveal failed or weak controls without the cost of an injury and should be investigated for preventive action.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Recordability does not determine whether a high-potential event should be investigated.
A name alone does not explain equipment, planning, supervision, or system conditions.
Waiting for harm sacrifices an opportunity to correct a serious failure before recurrence.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 22, near-miss relationship and investigation, pp. 527-535; OSHA Incident Investigation overview

questions.chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis
questions.stem: An investigation finds workers repeatedly reach through a point-of-operation opening to clear jams. Which corrective action is strongest?
options: Retrain workers to reach more carefully
Post a larger warning sign at the opening
Redesign the process so jams can be cleared without access to the hazard zone
Require supervisors to remind workers each shift
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A design change that eliminates hazardous access addresses the system and follows the hierarchy of controls more effectively than reminders.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Training alone leaves the physical opportunity for exposure unchanged.
A warning communicates the hazard but does not prevent access or eliminate the jam-clearing need.
Repeated reminders are an administrative control and remain dependent on behavior.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 22, countermeasures and investigation reports, pp. 524-536; OSHA root-cause guidance

questions.chapterTitle: Incident Causation, Investigation, and System Analysis
questions.stem: A corrective action is marked complete when a new procedure is issued. What additional evidence is most important before closing the investigation action?
options: A copy of the email announcing the procedure
The number of pages in the revised procedure
A statement that the responsible manager supports safety
Field verification that the change is implemented and effectively controls the identified cause
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Closure should require evidence that the action was implemented, used as intended, and reduced the causal risk without creating new hazards.
incorrectOptionExplanations: An email proves communication occurred but not implementation or effectiveness.
Document length does not demonstrate that the control addresses the cause.
General support is useful but is not objective evidence that the control works in practice.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 22, report of investigation and countermeasures, pp. 525-536
